Ibrahim Zadran | Afghanistan captain: [On the result and not putting enough runs on the board] Yeah, we didn’t get the result what we wanted. I would say we had three overs good start, then we didn’t contribute well. We given them back-to-back wickets and they have put pressure on us, and we batted well in the middle overs, but we didn’t put lots of runs on the board what we wanted. Their bowlers and their fielders did really well, I would say that run-out, was the turning point. Ishan Kishan grabbed the ball and threw it to the bowler. Yeah, I would say that was the turning point, they got the momentum. [On the two key wickets of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Azmatullah Omarzai] Yeah, exactly, they’re the best fielding side and as I mentioned, the way Ishan Kishan picked the ball and threw it perfectly, so it was the turning point, and Gurbaz didn’t have, his day. I would say he will come back stronger. We expect that from him and yes, India did well with the bowling and fielding department.

A dominant win has given India a 1-0 lead in the three-match T20I series. Jasprit Bumrah’s return has worked wonders, with India looking a class apart with the pace spearhead back in the mix. Abhishek Sharma’s explosive knock was another major highlight for the Men in Blue. He single-handedly took the game away from Afghanistan with some sensational hitting, inflicting serious damage along the way. Afghanistan will need to come up with much better plans to contain him when the two sides meet again on Tuesday. For now, this is Nikhil signing off on behalf of Sri Krishna and Harish. Take care!
